newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's military chief to visit Israel.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's military chief to visit Israel.

text.p: The chief of Turkey's armed forces, General Ismail Hakki Karadayi, is to visit Israel this month in a further sign of strengthening military cooperation between the two countries.
"The visit will take place, I believe, towards the end of the month," foreign ministry spokesman Sermet Atacanli told a news conference on Wednesday. He did not give any further details.

Moslem but secular Turkey and Israel have signed two military accords, which involve allowing Israeli jets on training flights in Turkish airspace and upgrading of the Turkish Air Force's fleet of F-4 Phantom jets by Israel.
The accords were condemned by Iran and many in the Arab world.

Ankara's closer links with Israel also drew strong protests at the time from Islamists in Turkey. Since become prime minister eight months ago Islamist Welfare Party leader Necmettin Erbakan has toned down his criticism.

However, an Islamist Welfare mayor was detained by police earlier this month after organising an anti-Israel protest near the capital. Tanks toured the district in an apparent warning to Islamists from Turkey's strictly secularist army.
